title: Conditional κ = 7.277211262868e-4 on #233's source-assisted row: the rank-3 whole-bank rung (self-contained, wired into CI)
body:
# Conditional κ = 7.277211262868e-4 on #233's source-assisted row: the rank-3 whole-bank rung, self-contained

**κ = 1819302815717/25·10¹⁴ = 7.277211262868e-4**, conditional, `binding = bit`, priced on a row
whose PR is **unmerged** (pinned by digest). A priced target on a scheduled row, not a witness.

## Change and mathematical scope

One self-contained package, a test module, and the package's own workflow. **No existing file is
edited.**

`research/complex-bank-run3/` prices the complex-side bank ladder above PR224's rung 2 — rungs 3
and 4 on the pinned profile (its padded width-66 schedule tops out at
`711599961413937/10^18` = 7.11599961413937e-4) — and then reads **PR233**
(`research/source-assisted-v4-layer`, head `109a857a329d18ed5552d5573f17ddfa886ae57f`) as a *row*.
On that row the ledger's first whole-bank family is **rank 3**, not rank 16: 29,964 rank-3
children per vertex, three registers each, so `3 · 89,892 = 269,676 = 66 · 4,086` three-copy
banks. Because `66 = 22 · 3`, the bank is exactly filled by 22 rank-3 blocks: **this rung needs no
padding at all**, and the T1 obligation the padded schedule exists to satisfy does not arise.

| the rung on #233's row | value |
| --- | --- |
| banks | 4,086 (1,362 per copy), 22 blocks × 3 registers, **padding 0** |
| retained ledger | stock 36,156 → 32,070; mass 2,382,336 → 2,112,660; children 635,067 → 545,175; families 20 → 19 |
| retained coarse saving | `417325324839139/5·10^17` = 8.346506496783e-4, the next 10⁻¹⁸ grid point up excluded |
| budget | the bit leaf `7.282510899902e-4` — **bit-bound**, so the complex supplier no longer binds |
| **κ** | **`1819302815717/25·10^14` = 7.277211262868e-4**, `binding = bit` |
| assembly | the unchanged 47-constraint assembly green at that budget, its own adjacent 10⁻¹⁸ point rejected |

| against | value | gain | asserted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this package's ladder top (the padded rung 4) | `711599961413937/10^18` = 7.11599961413937e-4 | **+2.2655%** | yes, by `verify.py`, offline |
| the frontier this package prices against (PR207) | `1366380910073/2·10^15` = 6.831904550365e-4 | **+6.5180%** | yes, by `verify.py`, offline |
| the record published on main (PR186) | `330942774629799/5·10^17` = 6.61885549259598e-4 | +9.95% | stated, dated |
| the highest other open claim at the time of writing (#251) | 7.10433687047883e-4 | +2.43% | stated, dated |

The two *asserted* rows cannot drift: `verify.py` re-derives both numbers from the pinned bytes
and asserts the comparisons. The two *stated* rows are dated observations of the queue and of
`main`, and are labelled as such.

## What proves it

```sh
cd research/complex-bank-run3
python3 -B verify.py                     # check: pins, rebuild, compare with certificate.json
python3 -B importer66.py --contract export-contract-rank3.json --self-test   # 13/13
cd references/pr219-run1 && python3 -B verify.py   # the vendored rung-1 package, in place
```

`verify.py` pins **62 files by sha256** — the 33 this package owns, the 16 the vendored rung-1
package of #219 carries, the 11 bodies of the bit drop and the six ranked heads of #233 — and
rebuilds the entire complex-side ladder: base, rung 2, rungs 3 and 4, both paid moments per rung,
the two 47-constraint assemblies with adjacent-grid rejection, the eligibility scan, the PR208
replica, the padded schedule, the instanced inventories, and all three export contracts (the
complex side's, the bit twin's with its 10-of-15 imported drop, and the rung's own). Then it
re-derives the rank-3 rung — the assignment from its addressing rule with zero padding, the
retained ledger, the bit leaf through #219's arithmetic, the point through the assembly rule — and
asserts both comparisons above. It reproduces PR207's, PR219's and PR224's published grid points
exactly.

The change adds exactly three things and edits nothing else:

* `research/complex-bank-run3/` — the package;
* `tests/test_complex_bank_run3.py` — nine isolated checks (the rebuild, all three contracts'
  self-tests, the refusal codes 2 and 4 with the rung publishing **0 of 6** required exports as
  bodies (ten bodies across them, all absent), the
  rank-3 price against the reviewed result, the rank-4 negative) plus three failure controls
  showing the digest gate fails closed on a tampered digest, a missing entry and a changed byte
  rather than passing vacuously; discovered by the existing `tests` group;
* `.github/workflows/complex-bank-ladder.yml` — the package's own job on 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14:
  `verify.py`, the vendored package's self-check, the three contracts' self-tests, then
  `git diff --exit-code`. It is path-filtered, so it costs nothing outside this package.

**Why a workflow instead of a Makefile target.** A target in the aggregate would be the local
convention, but `Makefile` and `.gitattributes` are *themselves recorded by other packages'
manifests* — `research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json` asserts the `Makefile` digest in `check_sources()`,
and the round-8, coordinated-frames, gaussian-parity and machine-transfer manifests record both
files. Editing either moves those digests and fails those groups' `git diff --exit-code`. A
path-filtered workflow of the package's own keeps this change to new files only, which is also why
it needs no `.gitattributes` carve-out: the package's byte-identical inputs are ordinary LF text
plus gzip containers, committed from an LF worktree and verified here by hashing the **blobs in
the index** (all 62 pinned paths) rather than the worktree.

No network, no Git credentials, no third-party packages, and no dependency on an unmerged branch
at run time: everything read is vendored and pinned, so the measurement re-runs in a clean clone
and in CI.

## It is row-dependent, and that is measured

`rank3stability.json`, re-derived by `verify.py → check_rank3_stability` and asserted:

* the rung exists on **two of the six ranked heads** of #233; the first four miss it by **one
  rank-3 child per copy** (nine registers over the ledger's three copies) — eligibility is the
  modular condition `22 | n₃`, a property of the row, not of the family;
* where it exists the **price is identical** (bit-bound), although the coarse saving differs;
* the **next rung's** eligibility is *not* stable — rank 4 is bankable only on the pinned head —
  and pricing it **moves κ not at all** (recorded as a negative);
* **no other width-66 row of this repository carries it**: nine distinct rows are scanned, and the
  pinned ladder row is eligible at `[11, 16, 20]` and misses rank 3 by 39 registers.

What the measurement does not cover: any head that does not exist yet (a new head is a new
measurement, not a silent pass), and rows outside this repository.

## What this does not claim

C1–C7 stay `OPEN` (the normalizer, the formal columns, the charts and prime witnesses, the envelope
parity and each child's frame/chain provenance) and R1–R4 are inherited verbatim from #219. No
importer exists for the rung: the row publishes **0 of 6** required exports as bodies — none of the
**ten bodies across them** (G1–G6) — so the gate refuses (exit 2) and reports in part when asked
(exit 4). That refusal is the correct answer, not a pass. The row's PR is
unmerged and pinned by digest, so a moved branch fails `check_manifest` closed and the measurement
must be re-taken. The 6,642 unpriced mixed tilings of the width-66 scan are not covered by the
measurement (two extremes per bank count are, and the artifact says so). Like every rung of this
ladder, this is a **conditional priced target**, not a witness, not an unconditional
multiplication theorem, not a practical multiplier, and not a Lean/kernel certificate.

## Attribution and provenance

Apache-2.0. The vendored inputs — PR219's rung-1 package, PR207's frontier certificate and PR233's
row certificate plus its earlier heads — are retained byte-identically with their notices and
credits (`NOTICE.md`, `SOURCE.json`); **PR233's contribution (chafreaky) is what this rung is priced
on** and is credited as such. Rung 2 and the ceiling argument are PR224's, the ladder and its
replica convention are PR208's, and the bank proof and engine chain are PR200/PR205/PR206/PR197/
PR184/PR168-v4/PR183/PR193's; nothing is re-implemented or restated as new. Prepared by Maxime
Fleury with Codebuff assistance.

**Supersedes #232**, which carries the same package without the rank-3 rung; #232 can be closed.
